recipes.name: Eclairs
ingredients_raw: 1 (5 ounce) package instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C). Lightly grease a cookie sheet; set aside.

Make choux pastry: Combine water and butter in a medium pot. Bring to a boil, stirring until butter melts completely. Reduce heat to low; add flour and salt at once. Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon until mixture leaves the sides of the pan and begins to form a stiff ball. Remove from heat and let dough cool for 10 minutes.

Add eggs to the dough, one at a time, beating well after each addition until incorporated. Using a spoon or pastry bag fitted with a No. 10 or larger tip, spoon or pipe dough onto the prepared cookie sheet in 1 1/2x4-inch strips.

Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C) and continue baking until the bottoms sound hollow when lightly tapped, about 20 more minutes. Transfer to a wire rack; pierce each eclair on the bottom with the tip of a knife to let steam out; let eclairs cool completely.

Make filling: Combine milk and pudding mix in a medium bowl according to package directions. Beat heavy cream with an electric mixer in a separate medium bowl until soft peaks form. Beat in confectioners’ sugar and vanilla. Fold whipped cream into pudding.
Cut tops off of cooled pastry shells with a sharp knife. Fill shells with pudding mixture and replace tops.

Make icing: Melt chocolate and butter in a medium saucepan over low heat. Stir in confectioners’ sugar and vanilla. Stir in hot water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until icing is smooth and has reached desired consistency. Remove from heat and cool slightly.
Drizzle chocolate icing over filled eclairs. Store in the refrigerator until serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Eclairs
raw_recipe.description: Delicious eclairs filled with homemade, rich pastry cream in a tender-crisp choux pastry topped with silky chocolate make you look like a pastry pro.

review.reviewBody:
This recipe is fabuolus, but it forgets to mention to peirce the ends of the eclair shells right after removing from the oven to release any steam. This keeps them from getting really soggy on the inside.

These eclairs have become a family favorite and everyone is convinced that I spend hours in the kitchen preparing these!

OK, first of all, these were incredible. I mean, they taste like they came fresh out of a bakery shop. A couple of notes though. First, if you don't have heavy cream or if you're just trying to reduce some of that calorie intake... replace the cream for 2 beaten egg whites (until it forms peaks), and add 1/2 cup confectioners sugar to it (instead of 1/4 cup that is supposed to be added to the cream). Add the vanilla as well. When you are done, fold it into the vanilla pudding and you'll have the perfect eclair filling that is creamy and absolutely divine. My second suggestion has to do with the chocolate glaze. What I got when following the recipe was hardly a glaze, it didn't stick to the eclair and was way too thick. So I added about two tablespoons of milk, 1/4 cup confectioners sugar, and 1 more ounce of chocolate. The glaze I made turned out perfect (and tasted amazing as well). Another suggestion, you should dip the top of the eclair into the chocolate before you cut it open. That way the chocolate is evenly spread over the top, instead of a gunky chocolate mess. Let the chocolate sit for a few minutes before you cut into it, I suggest even putting it into the freezer for a few minutes. That way, when you cut them in half, the chocolate won't get all over the place. All in all, this recipe was a slam dunk. The authenticity of these eclairs was certainly refreshing, and I can guarantee that I will be making these again.

I will be making this again, but I'll need to make sure I bake the pastry for the full amount of time; and I'll also need to beat the whipping cream longer, to the point of stiffer peaks rather than softer peaks. I took the pastry out earlier than I should have, worrying that I would over bake them. I think this is definitely one recipe to err on the over baking, rather than under baking. The recipe said to beat the whipping cream to soft peaks, but again, I think it's better to err on having stiffer peaks, rather than softer peaks. I'd like my filling to be firmer next time around. As far as the icing, I didn't make the icing that was on this recipe. I just made my own chocolate icing which consist of butter, salt, vanilla, powdered sugar, cocoa powder and milk. A nice thick, sweet frosting. I found it was easy to frost them by holding the cut top, and putting a big dollop of frosting on it, then spread it to the sides. You can extend it onto the other half of the shell if you would like, once the cap is back on. I also pierced the pastry once out of the oven. And like others had mentioned, they are even better if you take the time to refrigerate them.

would highly suggest not mixing water and chocolate, use heavy cream instead and instead of adding conf. sugar directly I would disolve it in the cream or it will become clumpy. all in all its a good recipe

A fabulous recipe! At least as good as any store bought eclairs I've ever tasted! In the half portion I made (4-5 eclairs), a few substitutions: Instead of icing sugar, I used Demerara; instead of pudding mix, just 1 cup whipping cream and 1 tbsp. Demerara, plus a touch (1/2 tsp.) of dissolved instant coffee (can use Nestlé's Ice Java syrup too); and I found the icing too sweet, so just used equal portions (1 tbsp.)chocolate chips, butter, and maple syrup. I made just a half portion of the recipe, for 4-5 eclairs, and it's perfect!

This was my first time making eclairs and choux pastry in general. The only changes I made were to switch out half a cup of the water for have a cup of milk. I also added about 3/4 cups of fresh strawberry purée to the cream filling and only put into cups of milk instead of 2 1/2. It was heavenly. I also had to use a star tip to pipe the eclairs as my rounded tip was far too small - however I think this turned out in my favour as this seemed to minimize the cracking of the dough while baking. I will definitely be trying this recipe again with other flavors!

Made these this morning for a brunch and they turned out beautifully. So much better than other recipes. However, a couple of notes that I think might be helpful. First, they were close to burned after the initial fifteen minutes. 450 seems a bit high. Second, they make a whole lot more than 9. I made 25 that were medium size. I would guess they were 1 inch by4 inches. They texture inside was perfect. I did not try the chocolate glaze, but filled instead with whipped cream/lemon curd and then topped with a basic powered sugar glaze. Delicious!

Came here looking for tips.... before I knew what I was doing I made the basic shells... while they were baking and cooling I made vanilla pudding (or another flavor sometimes) and iced them with thinned chocolate icing from a can ..... I was going for quick and easy and it worked....

Didn't work and I discovered why! They didn't puff and rise at all. I found another recipe (Better Homes & Gardens)that had the exact same ingredients, but the instructions tell you to let the dough cool for 10 minutes before adding the eggs. I tried that recipe after my flop with this one, and they worked perfectly. So you must let the butter/water/flour dough cool for 10 minutes before adding the eggs.

While I thought the end result of these eclairs were tasty, there were a couple very important steps left out of this recipe. The first thing is that you need to let the flour/butter/water/salt mixture cool for at least 10 minutes after cooking and before adding in the eggs, or you will end up with a mess of scrambled eggs. The second important step missing is that you need to pierce the eclair shells after baking to let the steam out--or you'll end up with soggy shells. The filling was just ok to me (I prefer real pastry cream), and I was not too fond of the chocolate icing. I had a bad feeling about adding water into anything chocolate, but I wanted to follow the recipe; and it came out grainy. Maybe cream would have worked better? Regardless, it was a fun recipe to try; but I think it would need some tweaking before I make it again. Thank you for sharing your recipe!

So this recipe has a couple of flaws. One being that when heating up the water and butter mixture it should never boil until the butter and water have become combined fully. Also the panade mix (water butter flour) should be completely cool before incorperating the eggs, this is so the eggs incorperate into the mix better. Also the ends of the eclairs should be pricked to ensure it does not become a soggy mess
Made this at home for my family. Comments say it's easy, IT IS NOT. Ended up with crispy balls. Chocolate flooding out. You can try, just don't if it's you first pat a choux recipe.
It was so easy and delicious!
Nice easy recipe they turned out perfect i will make these again 😋
First time making pate a choux, I'll try again. It wasn't bad, just not right.
Thank you for sharing your recipe 🙏. The only change I made was by using whipped cream.⭐
Amazing recipe.

Very easy to follow. I made some tweaks to this recipe; 1. Sifted the flour and salt into the pot for a smother result. 2. Let eggs come to slightly room temp, makes its easier to incorporate . 3. Rotated pan twice during each bake for a more even bake
Using this in a school assment , this makes it a lot easier . 👍
The #10 tip required is entirely too small. Whipped cream is absolutely unnecessary, and makes the filling runny. Sadly disappointed but I know what not to do next time.
